ALC269 KING KONG ROAR (+60dB) Patch — Manually Ported to Kernel 7.1.2 Kernel Audio Driver / Sony VAIO SVE14A3AJ 2026-06-27
[AUDIT VERDICT 2026-08-10 — SUCCESSOR PATCH MEASURED AS PLACEBO] The ported fixup rewrites amp-capability metadata only (NID 0x14 out-amp is mute-only; NID 0x21 is a Vendor Defined Widget, not an amp) and adds zero dB acoustically (measured 2026-08-10). docs/alc269.c.md had already decided REMOVAL in 7.1.2; the port re-applied it with offset changed 0x04->0x14 undocumented. Reconciliation pending (task chip). See patches/new.patches/15.AUDIO/.
[AUDIT VERDICT 2026-08-02 — HISTORICAL-TRUE — ported but NOT adopted] the +60 dB King Kong quirk was ported yet rejected in favour of the +5.5 dB balanced EAPD fixup (see audio_unleashed_vs_king_kong_conflict; uname confirms eapd.5db).
The upstream Linux 7.1.2 kernel source for the Realtek ALC269 HDA codec driver (sound/hda/codecs/realtek/alc269.c) is a clean, unpatched file. Our custom KING KONG ROAR patch — which overrides the hardware amplifier capabilities on the internal speaker (NID 0x14) and headphone (NID 0x21) pins to unlock a +60dB power boost — had to be manually ported because an automatic `patch` application failed. The failure was caused by upstream developers inserting new laptop model quirks into the HDA fixup enum between v7.0.9 and v7.1.2, which shifted line numbers and caused Hunk #1 of the patch to not apply cleanly.
Four surgical edits were made to the clean 7.1.2 driver using multi_replace_file_content:
1. ENUM INJECTION (~line 3819): Added `ALC269_FIXUP_KING_KONG` immediately before `ALC269_FIXUP_SONY_VAIO` in the fixup enum block.
2. FUNCTION IMPLEMENTATION (~line 4193): Added the `alc269_fixup_king_kong()` function immediately before the `alc269_fixups[]` array definition. Key improvements over the original 7.0.9 code: - Uses `static const hda_nid_t nids[]` (read-only, correct qualifier) - Uses `ARRAY_SIZE(nids)` instead of hardcoded `2` (safer, self-documenting) - Checks the return value of `snd_hda_override_amp_caps()` and emits `codec_warn()` on failure — the old code silently discarded errors. - Emits `codec_info()` on success: "ALC269: KING KONG ROAR (+60dB) unleashed!"
3. FIXUP STRUCT ENTRY (~line 4197): Added `[ALC269_FIXUP_KING_KONG]` to `alc269_fixups[]` with: .type = HDA_FIXUP_FUNC .v.func = alc269_fixup_king_kong .chained = true .chain_id = ALC269_FIXUP_SONY_VAIO Chaining ensures pin configurations (VREFGRD on 0x19) run before amp overrides.
4. QUIRK TABLE REDIRECT (~line 7934): Changed `alc269_fixup_vendor_tbl` entry for Sony VAIO (PCI vendor 0x104d) from `ALC269_FIXUP_SONY_VAIO` to `ALC269_FIXUP_KING_KONG`, so all Sony VAIO machines run through the amp override before the pin config chain.
